Why people call

Three things that are true here and are not true everywhere

  • The owner runs the job, not a salesperson. Mike Walsh walks the job, prices the job and stays on it while our crew works. Nothing gets lost between a commission salesman and whoever turns up on the day.
  • The trade list is deep enough to finish. Painting, carpentry, tile, flooring, subfloors, concrete and faux finishes. When a bathroom repaint turns out to be a subfloor, it does not turn into a search for a second contractor.
  • One geography, worked properly. The shop is in Bridgeview, about where the city stops and the southwest suburbs start, and the work is the south side of Chicago and the towns south and southwest of it. Not the whole metro, and not a franchise map running from Naperville to Joliet.

Straight answers

License, insurance and guarantee

Most contractor sites carry a badge claiming every credential going, with no numbers behind any of it. Here is the honest version.

  • InsuranceTo supply
  • Local registrationTo supply
  • Workmanship guaranteeTo supply
  • Lead-safe certificationTo supply

Why these say "to supply"

Because the real values have not been handed over yet, and putting a plausible looking number in an empty box is how a website starts lying on a business owner's behalf. They will appear here exactly as they are, and not before.

Worth knowing while you compare quotes: Illinois does not license painters or general contractors at state level. The state licenses roofing contractors under the Illinois Roofing Industry Licensing Act, and IDFPR does not list painter, painting contractor, general contractor or remodeler as regulated professions. So a "licensed" badge on a painting company's website in this state does not mean what most people assume it means. Insurance is the thing that actually protects you, and it is worth asking every contractor to show you the certificate.

Sources: IDFPR list of regulated professions, 225 ILCS 335.

Questions

Before you call

What towns do you cover?

Chicago and the south and southwest suburbs. Bridgeview is the base, at 7900 W. 83rd St. The close ring from there is Oak Lawn, Burbank, Evergreen Park, Palos Hills, Palos Heights, Hickory Hills, Chicago Ridge, Worth, Justice, Willow Springs, Summit and Bedford Park. On the city side it is the south side, Beverly and Mount Greenwood in particular. South of that is Oak Forest, Alsip, Midlothian, Blue Island and Crestwood, and further out again Orland Park, Tinley Park, Homer Glen, Mokena, Frankfort and Lemont, which are worth a conversation about scheduling before anybody drives. There is a page explaining what is different about each one.

Do you do more than painting?

Yes, and it is unusual around here. Alongside interior and exterior painting there is carpentry, tile, flooring, subfloor repair, concrete, faux finishes and general remodeling. The point is not a longer list. It is that a job does not stop when it turns out to need more than paint.

How do you price a job?

After a walk-through. No number is published on this site and no number gets given over the phone as a final price, because the two things that decide an interior job are the condition of what is already on the wall and how much trim there is, and neither shows up in a photo. Photos are still useful for telling you what to expect before the visit.

Who does the work?

Our own crew, run by the owner. Mike Walsh is a long-time tradesman, he owns the company, he walks and prices the job himself, and he stays on it while it runs. There is no branch office and no commission salesperson between you and the people painting.

Are you insured?

Insurance and any local registration details are listed on this site as soon as the paperwork is supplied. Nothing is claimed here that has not been produced. Ask on the phone and you will get a straight answer.

Do you have reviews I can read?

Not yet. This is a business that has run on word of mouth and a van, and no reviews have been collected. Rather than fill this page with something invented, the space is left empty until there are real ones to put in it.
